commits.message:
The shape-card spec finds the Effect shape block by its interface line

docs/effects.md's shape block is `interface Effect {` now that an effect may say when its frame next changes; the spec looked for `type Effect =` and found no card.

The stepped-ink cost test samples the step's first frame as it samples the rest

CI failed its one-sample assertion by 0.7%: a lone first-frame timing against a median of 59. Nine fresh signals' first frames are taken and their median compared, so one sample's jitter decides nothing. The contract asserted is unchanged.

systemClock.at ticks only once the clock reads the time

Review (medium, post-rebase) on PR #416.

A platform timer is due by the event loop's millisecond-truncated time,
so it ran while performance.now() still read under the time asked for,
by up to most of a millisecond. A Live waking at a frame's end then drew
the old frame again and waited again, at every boundary. The wait is now
rounded up and a timer that ran early is armed again for the remainder,
in the clock, once, for every host.

Style.toString's docstring claimed a round-trip through parse; meta,
anchor and nextChange have no spelling, so it now says it is the look.
A host can ask when what it draws next changes (rich-animation-xi28.6rs)

Markdown drops inline HTML where Rich does, and reads backslash escapes (rich-unfiled-791c.5r6q)

markdown-it-py's HTML_TAG_RE — a tag, comment, processing instruction,
declaration or CDATA section — is read inline and drawn as nothing. The
block kind for a lone tag and the inline rule now share one tag grammar.

The escape rule comes with it: markdown-it reads '\<' at the backslash
before html_inline sees the '<', so without it '\<span>' would draw '\'
where Rich draws '<span>'.

Unclosed openers scan to the end of the text from every '<', as
markdown-it-py's own regex does.

claude-sessions joins a command by its parent link and keeps all it says (rich-demos-k78j.0d5)

Medium review of #420. A local_command record's text is its content with the
command tags gone and the output tags unwrapped, so text outside those tags is
drawn rather than dropped. The record that runs a command and its output are
joined by the output's parentUuid instead of adjacency, so showing hidden
records no longer splits a command into two blocks.

claude-sessions draws a slash command once, and a system record's fields as read (rich-demos-k78j.0d5)

Review of #420. A slash command is the record that runs it and the
local_command record of its output, whose parent it is; the parser now joins
the two as it joins one message's chunks, so /clear and /login draw once, and a
prompt that runs a command with no output reads as its command line instead of
raw tags. Command tags have one reader for both record kinds.

A system record's own fields are typed unknown, as the JSON is, so each is read
by what it holds: a malformed one draws instead of failing the session, a
missing hook count is not claimed as zero, and a stop hook that prevented
continuation shows its reason (the stager now keeps preventedContinuation and
stopReason; re-staging added only those two fields). Output cut short by the
stager keeps its text, output carrying escape codes is decoded, and the body
follows selection like the title.

claude-sessions names every system record it draws (rich-demos-k78j.0d5)

A system record's rule was titled by its duration, which only turn_duration
records carry, so every slash command and stop hook drew as an empty '⚫ —'.
The parser now reads what each record says: a turn and how long it took, a
command's command line over its output, how many stop hooks ran over their
errors, and any other subtype by its name over its content.

The card's sessions are re-staged so they carry the fields that reading needs.
The re-run also brings in what the stager already keeps and the committed
staging predated: ten queued prompts, and the assistant records under them.

Markdown reads an HTML block where markdown-it does and draws it as Rich does, not at all (rich-unfiled-791c.e5pf) (#419)

* Markdown reads an HTML block where markdown-it does and draws it as Rich does, not at all (rich-unfiled-791c.e5pf)

CommonMark's seven HTML block kinds, matched as markdown-it matches them.
Every kind but a lone tag ends a paragraph, a table body and a lazy
continuation, through opensBlock. The block is kept as a token that draws
nothing, so a container ending in one does not read as ending in the
paragraph before it.

* An HTML block's end is the closing line or a blank one, named once; the table cites markdown-it-py (rich-unfiled-791c.e5pf)
